name: Daptomycin
executiveSummary: Lipopeptide against Gram-positives (incl. MRSA). Adult skin: **4 mg/kg IV every 24 h**; bacteremia/right-sided endocarditis: **6 mg/kg/day** (many centers **8–10 mg/kg**). **Do not use in pneumonia**. Monitor CPK.
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated skin and soft-tissue infections by Gram-positives.
- *S. aureus* bacteremia (incl. MRSA) and right-sided endocarditis.
- Alternative if vancomycin failure/intolerance.

## Precautions

- **Inactivated by pulmonary surfactant — contraindicated in pneumonia**.
- Myopathy / ↑ CPK — hold statins if possible; baseline and weekly CPK.
- Adjust in renal failure (every 48 h if CrCl <30).
- Incompatible with **D5W**.

> Adults: 2-min IV push possible; children: infusion only.

adulto.dose: Skin/soft tissue: **4 mg/kg IV every 24 h**. Bacteremia / right-sided endocarditis: **6 mg/kg every 24 h**. Intensified (ID): **8–10 mg/kg every 24 h**. CrCl <30: same mg/kg **every 48 h**.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute with SW (rest ~10 min; do not shake hard). Adults: IV 2 min or dilute in NS over **30 min**. NS only.
adulto.notes: Watch for myalgias and peripheral neuropathy.

pediatrico.dose: 1–<2 years: often **10 mg/kg every 24 h**. 2–6 years: **9–10 mg/kg/day**. 7–11 years: **7 mg/kg/day**. 12–17 years: **5 mg/kg/day** (skin) or **7 mg/kg** (bacteremia) — follow label by indication.
pediatrico.administration: IV infusion **30–60 min** in NS (no push in children).

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~24 h room temp / ~48 h refrigerated.
- Diluted in NS: ~48 h refrigerated.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

↑ CPK, myalgia, eosinophilic pneumonia (rare), headache, diarrhea, anemia, ↑ transaminases.
